props.title: Stardust
props.initialSlug: A fallen star sparks a magical quest for true love

sections.content: Stardust brilliantly adapts Neil Gaiman's fantasy novel into a swashbuckling romance that channels the spirit of The Princess Bride (1987). Director Matthew Vaughn infuses the tale with both whimsy and edge - a balance he'd later perfect in Kick-Ass (2010) and X-Men: First Class (2011). The film follows Tristan's journey across a magical wall into the realm of Stormhold, mixing star-crossed love with supernatural adventure. Michelle Pfeiffer delivers a deliciously wicked performance as the youth-obsessed witch Lamia, while Robert De Niro subverts his tough-guy image as the cross-dressing sky pirate Captain Shakespeare.

sections.content: The film stands out for its stellar ensemble cast, including Claire Danes as the fallen star Yvaine, Charlie Cox before his Daredevil (2015) fame, and Mark Strong as the ruthless Prince Septimus. The practical effects and imaginative world-building create a tangible fairy tale universe that feels more authentic than the CGI-heavy approaches of contemporaries like The Golden Compass (2007) or Eragon (2006). Vaughn's direction maintains momentum through multiple plotlines while building genuine emotional stakes.

Stardust shares DNA with other British fantasy films like Time Bandits (1981) and Labyrinth (1986), combining dry humor with genuine wonder. The film's treatment of magic feels grounded despite its fantastical elements, creating rules and consequences that give weight to the supernatural elements. This approach influenced later fantasy adaptations like Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children (2016) and The House with a Clock in Its Walls (2018). SUBHEAD: The Revival of Romantic Fantasy

sections.content: Stardust helped spark a revival of romantic fantasy films that blend adventure with love stories, paving the way for movies like Enchanted (2007) and The Shape of Water (2017). Its success demonstrated audiences' appetite for fantasy that doesn't take itself too seriously while still delivering genuine emotion and spectacle. The film's influence can be seen in later works like Maleficent (2014) and Cinderella (2015), which similarly reimagine fairy tale tropes with modern sensibilities.
